fact: Chief Justice Shivute said the Supreme Court remains entirely paper-based and efforts to extend e-justice to it are under way, with a task force defining an integrated electronic case management system.

The Uganda Judiciary reports that Namibia is preparing to roll out its own Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS), and a 15-member Namibian delegation benchmarked Uganda's ECCMIS in May 2025.

Government Notice 249 of 2017 (Supreme Court rules, in operation 15 November 2017) defines e-justice as the internet-based system for delivering process and maintaining court case files, whose start date the Chief Justice is to set by Gazette notice.

Rule 23 of the Supreme Court rules requires parties, from the date the Chief Justice sets, to file court process electronically through e-justice as registered users, and lets law firms register as users; rule 24 says the system is designed to serve 24 hours a day.
The NACM nomination describes Namibia eJustice as a fully implemented end-to-end electronic filing and case management system for the Supreme Court and High Court civil stream.
The nomination says Namibia eJustice connects the Supreme Court and High Court with legal practitioners for e-filing and commencement of case files.
